label: Does an impersonal source explain the actual selection or only a permitted range?
summary: See docs/notes/optimal-creation-choice.md sections 59-64 (#2145 Lane 2). Verified results: 54e1279c (choice-cell determination laws: an invariant explanans explains exactly the realized range; selecting a contingent outcome requires a contingent explanans level that no invariant level sees to; the standard reads only cells (law 7, definitional) and any outcome-fine level meets it (law 8); the #1953 decomposition), f66e83d4 (matched four-frame table: necessary manifestation, invariant D-range frame, permissive frame, exercise frame; account assignments are interpretive), 72c06088 (giving-level omission scopes strictly ordered; a necessarily productive source keeps individual and replacement omission and loses giving-level total refraining; a fixed giver gives each recipient wherever it exists; the section 56 replacement table certified with ActualAbsenceByWithholding; STIT controls pointwiseNotJoint and tiedNoEmptyChoice registered), cdde5406 (the #1953 complete-decision fork with Mathlib Maximal: an undominated-decision policy with a creation above omission never chooses omission, yet can avoid each creation), adb23c1c (0050b6ed from the world-level total-noncreation power a8dedf3f, Euclidean access 62b4a40a and monotone powers 6fdd3f60), 44e8200e (a8dedf3f and 0050b6ed independent as typed; only the bundle with both bridges is stronger; each bridge needed, the Euclidean control with a necessary holder). Finding: the determination standard on cells does not discriminate selection from re-description, so the selection step stays open. Decision: 0050b6ed needs only the replacement scope. Semantic challenge at 249d18648 found 5 P1 and 8 P2 issues; all repaired in the same PR.
blocker: Not blocked for the assigned formal questions. The determination standard on choice cells is met by any outcome-fine level, so it cannot separate rational adoption, actualization, generative exercise or a bare re-description of the outcome. A discriminating test needs a standard individuating the explanans independently of the outcome partition, or pro tanto favouring by apprehended content (connects to the Investigation 2 finite-measure test), a warranted permission boundary that makes omission undominated, or the #1380 supervenience obligation of a knowing invariant source.

current_assessment.scope: Range versus actual selection under one determination standard; omission scope of the GOD_4 joint-absence power
current_assessment.assessment: Under the determination standard on choice cells (SELECTING_AN_OUTCOME_2), invariant levels of any account explain exactly the range, and a contingent selection is met only by an outcome-fine level, trivially; so this standard does not discriminate and the selection step remains open, with favouring and apprehended content untested. 0050b6ed needs only the replacement scope; as typed, with PowerFor free, a structural surrogate satisfies it with a necessarily productive source, and the will routes discriminate through their other premises (fdd2b1cf, 65e0179f; a065c332, a9776d21).
current_assessment.next_test: Find a selection standard that individuates the explanans independently of the outcome partition, or test pro tanto favouring by apprehended content (Investigation 2 finite-measure test); test a warranted permission boundary that makes omission undominated.
current_assessment.evidence: Proposed assessment in draft PR-2154. The six results passed the focused Lean build, binding check, Comparator and NanoDa. Independent semantic challenge ran at 249d18648c7cb6bdcc2856bbb6a17a4d30bbf28e (5 P1, 8 P2, all repaired in the PR); re-check of the repaired head pending.
current_assessment.supersedes: None. It specifies the selection and omission-scope comparison of sections 39, 56 and 57 without revising their overall judgments.
